source: Post-audit enacted laws and substantive 2026 codification registry
description: Publication metadata for enacted laws whose current Code dispositions are maintained by the substantive current-law overlay rather than the completed 270-law audit action ledger.

actions.description: National-security eligibility provisions are classified to 50 U.S.C. §§ 5001–5007.
Commerce, trade, intellectual-property, and labor transfer provisions are classified to 15 U.S.C. §§ 10001–10011.
Conflict-of-interest provisions are consolidated into 18 U.S.C. § 205 as new subsections (k)–(n).
Commissioned-service staffing and continuity provisions are classified to 5 U.S.C. §§ 2501–2504.
Whistleblower and oversight protections are classified to 5 U.S.C. §§ 2308–2314.
Express repeals and transition, savings, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as statutory history or notes where appropriate.

laws.title: Metropolitan Police Department Public Safety and Property Reform Act

actions.description: Permanent MPD public-safety and property-authority provisions are classified to 40 U.S.C. §§ 9701–9716.
Short-title, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as notes at 40 U.S.C. § 9701.
Federal law-enforcement communications and coordination provisions are classified to 6 U.S.C. §§ 1801–1815.
Short-title, severability, and effective-date provisions are retained as notes at 6 U.S.C. § 1801.

laws.title: United States Capitol Police Reform and Accountability Act

actions.description: Permanent Capitol Police organization, governance, jurisdiction, protective-service, enforcement, use-of-force, oversight, access, emergency, political-neutrality, and penalty provisions are classified to 2 U.S.C. §§ 7001–7019.

The Act expressly repeals the Uniformed Capitol Police Act of 2023 and the United States Capitol Police Technical Corrections Act, terminates authority dependent solely on those enactments, and supersedes inconsistent continuing law, rule, regulation, or order. Existing archived law identities are preserved where the historical archive contains conflicting public-law numbering.

actions.treatment: short-title, severability, rule-of-construction, and effective-date notes
actions.description: Short-title, severability, rule-of-construction, and effective-date/transition provisions are retained as statutory notes at 2 U.S.C. § 7001.
